name: certen-policy-signer
description: Headless policy-gated signer for Accumulate — your off-chain policy engine decides, your key signs, and nothing signs without an approval
//bin: Two names for one binary: the short one is current, the long one is what earlier deployments call it. Removing the alias would break an existing install for no benefit.
//files: The published package is the esbuild bundle plus the two configs and the reference examples — the things you need to RUN it. src/ and test/ stay in the repo. Note the bundle already contains the patched accumulate.js (see postinstall below), so an npm consumer needs no patch step of their own.

scripts.//prepare: Patch, then build. `prepare` runs on `npm install` in a clone (a plain clone has no dist/, so without this the bin is a dead path) and before `npm publish` — but NOT when a consumer installs the published tarball, which is exactly what we want: the accumulate.js patch is a DEV-TREE fix that the esbuild bundle then inlines, so a consumer inherits the fix in dist/ and has nothing to patch. This was a `postinstall`, which npm does run for installed dependencies; there it found no node_modules/accumulate.js to patch and printed a warning that read like a broken install. --if-possible: a production or dependency-only install has nothing to build, and that is not an error.
